_owner: seo-image-optimizer owns this file: the indexability failure-mode scan on images that already exist on a page, and the alt attribute VALIDITY and decorative-versus-content split. It runs alongside the existing filename, image URL, and alt alignment work in Phase 5 and does not replace it. What alt must SAY (describe what the image shows, never a keyword list, and the core-term overlap exemption) is already fixed by Phase 5 of the skill and by the used-word ledger from seo-onpage-strategy; this file adds only the empty-alt decision and the markup-validity check on top of it. Image briefs, prompts, exact dimensions, the three-ratio delivery set, sitemap declaration completeness, and the licensing-fields exception belong to seo-image-production. Image structured data, licensing markup, and badge eligibility belong to aiso-schema. Section order inside the page body belongs to seo-article-anatomy. Video thumbnails belong to seo-video.

scope_and_deference.in_scope: Whether an image as currently delivered CAN be indexed, and whether its alt attribute is both correctly classified and valid markup.
scope_and_deference.out_of_scope: Building the image, choosing its dimensions, declaring it in a sitemap, and the three-ratio delivery set: seo-image-production owns those at build time inside a declared content pipeline. Structured data that carries the image, and any licensing or badge markup: aiso-schema owns that. Where the page's sections sit relative to one another: seo-article-anatomy owns that.
scope_and_deference.lifecycle_split: This scan is diagnostic and runs on what is already published. The same placement rule applied at build time, before the package ships, is stated once by seo-image-production. Report the defect here; hand the rebuild to that skill when the image belongs to a declared pipeline.

indexability_failure_modes.rule: Run all six checks on every image the client needs found in image results. Any one of them firing is sufficient to explain a zero-impression image, so record which one fired rather than a bare 'not indexed' verdict.

modes.condition: The image is delivered only as a CSS background.
modes.why_it_fails: Only the HTML is parsed for images, so an image that exists solely in a stylesheet is never seen and never indexed.
modes.fix: Require a real img element for any image that must be found. A background image may stay a background image only when it is decoration nobody needs to search for.
modes.evidence: Quote the CSS rule and confirm no img element carries the same asset.

modes.why_it_fails: A lazy-loaded image may be absorbed late or not at all, so its presence in the rendered view is not proof it was collected.
modes.fix: Mitigate on two fronts: declare the image in an image sitemap so it is discoverable without depending on the render, and deliver it responsively through a picture element with multiple sources or an img with a srcset. Neither mitigation alone is the fix.
modes.evidence: Name the lazy-load mechanism found and state whether a sitemap entry and a responsive source set both exist.

modes.condition: The image sits in a sidebar, a header, or footer navigation.
modes.why_it_fails: Images in those regions are treated as decoration and ignored, whatever their alt text says.
modes.fix: An image that carries the page's subject belongs high in the body and above the fold. Moving it out of the chrome is the fix; rewriting its alt is not.
modes.evidence: Name the region the image was found in and the position of the first in-body image.

modes.condition: Hotlink protection, or a server setting that blocks cross-origin display, prevents the file from rendering when it is requested from anywhere other than the site itself.
modes.why_it_fails: An image that cannot be displayed off-site cannot appear in image results at all.
modes.fix: Allow the image to be displayed cross-origin, or accept that it will not appear. Decide this deliberately per directory rather than leaving a blanket rule in place by accident.
modes.evidence: Request the image URL without a same-site referrer and record the status code and body returned.

modes.condition: The image is served from a different top-level domain than the page displaying it.
modes.why_it_fails: The association between page and image is weakened when the two do not share a top-level domain.
modes.fix: Host the image on the same top-level domain as the page that displays it. A subdomain or path-based asset host on that same top-level domain is inside the rule.
modes.evidence: Record the page host and the image host side by side.

modes.condition: The exported source file still carries an embedded thumbnail.
modes.why_it_fails: Embedded thumbnails inflate file size and break some compression pipelines, so the file arrives heavier than it should and may fail processing outright.
modes.fix: Disable embedded thumbnails at export time, before the file enters any optimisation step.
modes.evidence: Record the presence of an embedded thumbnail in the source file and the file size before and after removal.

alt_decision_tree.rule: Classify every image as decorative or content BEFORE writing any alt text. The two classes take opposite treatment and getting the class wrong cannot be repaired by better wording.

decorative.examples: Spacers, borders, and ornamental elements that carry no information a reader would miss.
decorative.required: An EMPTY alt attribute, or no alt attribute at all.
decorative.forbidden: Writing descriptive alt text for a decorative image. It is wrong, not merely unnecessary, because it pushes noise into the page's context.
decorative.audit_verdict: A decorative image carrying descriptive alt is a defect and is listed as one.

content.definition: Any image a reader would lose information by not seeing.
content.required: A descriptive alt attribute, then the validity check below.
content.content_rules_owner: What the words must say stays under Phase 5 of this skill and the used-word ledger from seo-onpage-strategy. Do not restate or reopen those rules here.

alt_attribute_validity.rule: Correct words in an invalid attribute deliver nothing. Check the markup itself on every content image, not just the text.

checks.failure: Without quotes, everything after the first word is lost and the rest of the tag is misparsed.

checks.test: The value contains no unescaped apostrophes or quotation marks.
checks.failure: CMS-generated alt text carrying a raw apostrophe or quotation mark invalidates the tag. This is the common source because the text is assembled by the platform, not typed by hand.
checks.fix: Escape the symbol or write it as an entity. Check CMS-generated alt specifically; hand-written alt is not where this fault usually starts.

alt_attribute_validity.verdict: An image whose alt fails either check is reported as an invalid attribute, not as missing alt. The two send the client to different fixes.

title_attribute_rule.default: The title attribute is redundant when alt is present. Do not add one.
title_attribute_rule.when_a_system_forces_one: Mirror the alt words rather than inventing a second description.
title_attribute_rule.hard_stop: Never let a forced title render with dashes substituted for spaces. A dash-separated title is a filename leaking into a user-visible field and is reported as a defect.

scan_output.rows: One row per image scanned, carrying: image file, page URL, failure mode fired or none, alt class (decorative or content), alt validity (valid, unquoted, unescaped symbol, or not applicable), title attribute state, evidence.
verdict_rules: A failure mode fires only on evidence read in this run. A fetch that failed is 'could not verify', never a fired mode.
An image that passes all six modes and carries a valid alt is a pass and gets no recommendation.
Where the image belongs to a declared content pipeline, name seo-image-production as the owner of the rebuild instead of proposing a build change here.
